title: OSCE dissolves the Minsk Group created to mediate the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict
body:
The OSCE announced on Monday, 1 September 2025 that the Minsk Group had been dissolved. The decision was reached by consensus of all 57 OSCE participating states. The OSCE had established the Minsk Group in 1992 to support a negotiated, peaceful resolution of the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, and it had served as the main mediator between Azerbaijan and Armenia.

The dissolution followed a declaration signed in Washington on 8 August 2025 by Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in the presence of US President Donald Trump, in which they agreed to dissolve the group. Azerbaijan had made the group's dissolution a central demand in peace talks. Before the decision, Nagorno-Karabakh Armenians had appealed to OSCE states to delay dissolution until strong guarantees existed for the safe return of displaced Armenians.

OSCE Secretary General Feridun Sinirlioglu called the dissolution a historic development showing what diplomacy can achieve. Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen, who chaired the Minsk Group, congratulated both countries. Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry welcomed the move as an important step and said the group had become redundant. In 2023 Azerbaijan retook control of the enclave in a rapid offensive, and Armenian officials said over 100,000 ethnic Armenians fled.
